subject: Learning Methods
title: Time-of-Day Effects on Learning
description: A quick, practical guide to Time-of-Day Effects on Learning.

hook.text: Memory for facts peaks in the late morning. Creative problem-solving peaks in the early evening.

buildup.text: Analytical tasks requiring focused attention align with peak cortisol. Creative tasks benefit from slight fatigue.

discovery.text: Time-of-Day Effects on Learning reveals the principle that makes the learning stick.

twist.text: Most people schedule creative work for their peak alertness and routine work for their tired hours.

climax.text: Time-of-Day Effects on Learning matters because durable learning depends on method, not just effort.

punchline.text: Focus when sharp. Create when tired. Timing transforms results.

quiz.question: Why is slight fatigue beneficial for creative problem-solving?
options: Tired brains process visual information better
The mental filter weakens, allowing unusual associations to form
Fatigue increases dopamine which fuels creativity
